catalog_task.title: Update Automation Catalog
catalog_task.prompt:
Update my automation catalog across all accessible businesses, client projects and personal projects.

Trigger
Run when the saved cloud schedule starts. Use the scheduled Monday's date in America/Los_Angeles. The work must not depend on my computer being awake.

Inputs
Read the Automation Catalog skill and its linked references from private GitHub repository RachaelQuisel/Skills. Use commit 780d1e3a21bcc3bf2e930f31417824ebf23c5fa6 and path plugins/automation-catalog/skills/automation-catalog/SKILL.md. This saved copy is the fallback when the installed skill is unavailable. Use the current installed /auto and /voice-align skills when available.
Read connected workflow definitions, scheduled tasks, GitHub code, Airtable automations, Google Drive project documents and Slack references. Check other providers only when connected and authorized.
Use La Maison Slack #automations for the overall status report: channel C0C7XQK3TTR, workspace T0AT819U2UQ, connection link_6acb11be38d48191845021d2cc6cd53b.

What happens
1. Use ACATALOG:YYYY-MM-DD as the label for this scheduled occurrence. Read relevant channel messages and all replies in its status thread. If a verified COMPLETE, PARTIAL or FAILED final report already exists, return its link without running again. If another run may be active, report blocked instead of starting a second worker.
2. Allow at most five total attempts, including the first. This is one budget for the whole occurrence, not five attempts per source. Before each attempt, save ATTEMPT n/5 in the status thread and read it back. If the count cannot be read or recorded, stop and report the blocker. On resume, use the largest recorded count. Never reset it, start attempt six or launch another run to bypass it.
3. Retry only problems that may clear on retry. Stop early for denied access, missing authorization or unclear destinations. If a write times out, check whether it succeeded before retrying. Keep write receipts and resume only unfinished work.
4. Search all accessible projects, not just La Maison. Read all relevant result pages. Record sources that are denied, unavailable, not checked or cut short. Do not claim a complete search while gaps remain.
5. Match each workflow by business, provider and stable identifier. For code, use its repository and entry point. Reuse existing guides and Slack messages. Skip unchanged content. Keep plans, reviewed code, enabled schedules and observed runs separate.
6. Apply /auto to each distinct workflow. Write Trigger, Inputs, What happens and Outputs in plain English. Add category, workflow type, tool and run tags. Update related current documents. Append to existing running updates. Preserve necessary business facts and source links.
7. For La Maison, reuse the #automations index thread 1791723995.673909 and its guide messages. For other businesses, verify the existing document home, Slack workspace, channel and audience. If a destination is unclear, hold that Slack write and continue other work. Keep each business's private details in its own project. The La Maison status thread may contain safe overall counts and blockers, but no other client's private workflow content.
8. Change only documentation. Do not run, repair, enable, pay through or reschedule any discovered workflow. Do not merge pull requests. Keep this weekly task active after a failed occurrence.

Outputs
Always post a final report in the occurrence's status thread, even when nothing changed. Include ACATALOG:YYYY-MM-DD and one result:
- COMPLETE: all in-scope work finished.
- PARTIAL: useful work was saved, but search or publication gaps remain.
- FAILED: the run was blocked or used all five attempts.

Include attempts used out of five; counts found, documented, saved, posted and unchanged; search gaps; known reasons for failure; blockers; one next step; and verified links safe for this channel. Base failure reasons on evidence. Say unknown when the cause is unknown. Report immediately when stopping early or after the fifth attempt. Read back the final Slack report. If Slack delivery fails, return the full report here in ChatGPT and say it was not delivered. Never claim success without a verified result.

Manual test authorized for October 11, 2026: if invoked on that local date, use ACATALOG-MANUAL:2026-10-11 instead of the scheduled Monday label. Keep its attempt budget separate from Monday. Use all other discovery, publication and reporting rules.

report_check_task.title: Check Catalog Reports
report_check_task.prompt:
Check whether Update Automation Catalog produced its final report. Do not run or retry the catalog.

Trigger
Run when the saved cloud schedule starts. Check the current scheduled Monday in America/Los_Angeles.

Inputs
Read task 6acb928d16bc8191ae1716cfe40da199. Check whether it is enabled and when it last ran, if this information is available.
Read La Maison Slack #automations: channel C0C7XQK3TTR, workspace T0AT819U2UQ, connection link_6acb11be38d48191845021d2cc6cd53b.
Read all relevant pages and replies for ACATALOG:YYYY-MM-DD. This label identifies the scheduled Monday's run.

What happens
1. Look for a verified COMPLETE, PARTIAL or FAILED final report. A start note or ATTEMPT note is not a final report.
2. If more than five catalog attempts are recorded, alert that the attempt limit was exceeded. Do not start another attempt.
3. If the catalog task is disabled, alert once for this occurrence. Do not enable it.
4. If a verified COMPLETE report exists, stay quiet. If PARTIAL or FAILED already explains the blockers, do not repeat it.
5. If no final report exists by this check, send a short alert. State whether a start was seen. Include the known attempt count and available scheduler evidence. Say the cause is unknown unless logs prove it. A missing start may mean the task did not run. A start without a report may mean it is still running, stalled or unable to report. Time alone does not prove failure.
6. Use ACATALOG-WATCH:YYYY-MM-DD as the alert label. Before sending, check whether the same alert was already delivered. Do not send a duplicate.
7. Allow at most five total alert-delivery attempts, including the first. Save and read back the delivery count in the approved run thread when it is available. If the count cannot be read or recorded, stop Slack attempts and report here. Before retrying a timed-out write, check whether it succeeded. Do not retry denied access or an unclear destination.
8. Read back the sent alert. If Slack is unavailable, return the full alert here in ChatGPT and say Slack delivery failed.

Outputs
Send an alert to #automations only when action is needed. Include the run label, what was observed, evidence, known attempt count, blockers, one next step and a verified message link when delivery succeeds. Keep other clients' private details out of the alert.
This check depends on the cloud scheduler and Slack. Do not promise that it can notify me during an outage affecting both.

Manual test authorized for October 11, 2026: if invoked on that local date, inspect ACATALOG-MANUAL:2026-10-11 and use ACATALOG-WATCH-MANUAL:2026-10-11 for an alert. For this manual test, if a final report is not present yet, report that it is still pending instead of treating the scheduled deadline as missed.

limits.enforcement: agent instructions with durable Slack count; not a hard scheduler cap
